changes.before: New users submit a document type absent from evaluation. What is the sound next step?
changes.after: When real inputs change, check whether old evaluation results still apply.

before: A model evaluated on one population may encounter different inputs later. Distribution shift means the data or its relationship to the target has changed.
A document classifier trained on short English notes may receive long multilingual scans after release. Its old evaluation result does not establish performance on those new inputs.

Worked example: the original evaluation has 100 typed notes and no scanned pages. A later batch is mostly scans. Measure performance on a labeled sample of the new cases before assuming the old result transfers.

Monitor meaningful input and outcome changes, then investigate whether evaluation data still represents actual use. A change in inputs is a signal to examine, not automatic proof that every prediction is wrong.
Changed situation: New users submit a document type absent from evaluation. What is the sound next step?
New evidence should address the changed population. Neither blanket confidence nor blanket failure follows from the old score.
after: Distribution shift means the data, or its relationship to the target answer, has changed. A model may face different conditions from those used to evaluate it.
A document sorter was evaluated only on typed notes. A scanned page is a different kind of input, so the old score does not establish how well it handles scans.
Collect a suitable sample of the new cases with checked target answers. Evaluate the model on them before treating the old result as evidence for these new conditions.
Watch changes in inputs and results over time. Check whether evaluation data still reflects how the model is being used.
A changed input type is a reason to investigate. It does not prove that every new prediction will fail, or that the old score will still hold.
